cancer_indication: Deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer
moa: Talazoparib is a potent small-molecule inhibitor of PARP-1/2 that blocks repair of single-strand DNA breaks and is a highly potent PARP-trapping inhibitor that stabilizes PARP–DNA complexes. Accumulated DNA lesions convert into toxic double-strand breaks during replication; in BRCA1/2-dependent homologous recombination (HR)-deficient tumor cells, these breaks cannot be efficiently repaired, leading to replication fork collapse, genomic instability, and apoptosis (synthetic lethality). It is clinically used in HER2-negative breast cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutations.

REACTOME_HDR_THROUGH_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBIN.description: Homologous recombination repair (HRR) is a BRCA1/2-dependent pathway that repairs DNA double-strand breaks and supports accurate genome maintenance during replication.
REACTOME_HDR_THROUGH_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBIN.interpretation:
HRR status is a central determinant of breast tumor DNA repair capacity and influences vulnerability to DNA damage accumulation when repair is compromised.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- gBRCA1/2 or broader HRD ↓ impairs high-fidelity DSB repair. Talazoparib induces PARP trapping and replication-associated damage; HR-deficient breast tumour cells cannot repair this, leading to synthetic lethality and strong clinical benefit (EMBRACA, gBRCA HER2-negative ABC). (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some gBRCA/HRD breast cancers can show a transcriptional HRR signature (damage-response induction) yet remain functionally HR-defective → still PARPi-sensitive.

MSigDB: REACTOME_HDR_THROUGH_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION_HRR (M27570; Reactome R-HSA-5685942); Reactome R-HSA-5685942 (GSEA MSigDB); FDA TALZENNA label (PARP1/2 inhibitor; PARP-DNA complexes) (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High functional HRR capacity (HR-proficient/HDR-intact tumors) repairs PARPi-associated lesions and blunts synthetic lethality → reduced talazoparib benefit.
Reactome R-HSA-5685942 (Reactome); NEJM EMBRACA talazoparib in gBRCA breast cancer (clinical context) PMID:30110579; NCT01945775 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Baseline HRR down/HRD (gBRCA1/2 or HR pathway defects) creates reliance on PARP-mediated repair; PARP inhibition + trapping produces lethal DNA damage.
NEJM EMBRACA PMID:30110579; DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1802905; NCT01945775 (PubMed); PARP trapping mechanism (jpet.aspetjournals.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: HRD tumors can still resist PARPi via HR-independent mechanisms (e.g., fork protection/DDR rewiring or low PARP1 dependence), despite low HRR signatures.
PARPi resistance mechanisms review (MDPI); (HRR pathway definition) Reactome R-HSA-5685942 (Reactome)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (signature-level): Talazoparib-induced DNA damage can upregulate HRR gene expression, but if HR remains nonfunctional (core defect persists) cells still die.
FDA TALZENNA label (DNA damage via PARP inhibition/trapping) (FDA Access Data); Reactome R-HSA-5685942 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Acquired resistance can occur via HRR restoration (e.g., BRCA1/2 reversion) or end-resection changes (53BP1/Shieldin loss), raising effective HRR → PARPi resistance.
BRCA reversions: PMID:32699032 (PubMed); Shieldin/53BP1 biology: PMID:30224654 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent HRR deficiency under PARP inhibition maintains synthetic lethality (unrepaired lesions → DSBs/collapse) → sensitivity.
PARP trapping / cytotoxicity mechanism (jpet.aspetjournals.org); NEJM EMBRACA PMID:30110579 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even if HRR remains low, resistance can emerge via drug exposure issues (efflux) or pathway bypass (e.g., tolerance of lesions) → resistant phenotype.
PARPi resistance review (MDPI); ABC transport interactions (context for exposure) PMID:36430819 (PubMed)

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Programmed cell death signaling pathways that execute apoptosis in response to irreparable cellular damage, including DNA damage.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation:
Apoptotic competence shapes whether breast cancer cells undergo cell death after severe DNA damage and checkpoint activation.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- In talazoparib-sensitive tumors, accumulated DNA damage and replication stress trigger mitochondrial apoptosis (caspase activation, pro-apoptotic signalling). However, “high baseline apoptosis” is not a standard predictive biomarker; what matters is an intact apoptotic machinery that can be engaged once damage accumulates. This pathway is best tagged as mechanism-of-action / on-treatment rather than as a baseline Up/Down predictor. (SpringerLink)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: “Apoptosis-primed” tumors (high pro-apoptotic readiness) more readily execute cell death after PARPi-induced DNA damage.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS (M5902) (GSEA MSigDB); FDA TALZENNA label (DNA damage → decreased proliferation/cell death) (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Bulk “apoptosis” signatures can coexist with strong anti-apoptotic blocks (IAP/BCL2-family dominance), limiting execution despite apparent pathway upregulation.
Hallmark definition (apoptosis/caspases) (GSEA MSigDB); PARPi resistance overview (MDPI)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Even with low baseline apoptosis transcription, profound HRD can still trigger rapid DNA-damage–driven apoptosis upon PARP trapping.
NEJM EMBRACA PMID:30110579 (PubMed); PARP trapping mechanism (jpet.aspetjournals.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low apoptotic competence (e.g., impaired caspase pathway / strong survival programs) reduces the likelihood of death after DNA damage → resistance.
MSigDB HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS (GSEA MSigDB); PARPi resistance review (MDPI)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Talazoparib drives DNA damage (PARP inhibition + trapping), which activates DDR and downstream apoptosis → response.
FDA TALZENNA label (FDA Access Data); NEJM talazoparib breast cancer PMID:30110579 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Apoptotic signaling may be initiated but blocked at execution (e.g., caspase inhibition/mitochondrial block), yielding non-response despite “up” signature.
MSigDB HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS (GSEA MSigDB); PARPi resistance review (MDPI)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (bulk-tissue effect): In strong responders, tumor-cell depletion can reduce measured apoptosis transcripts over time despite drug sensitivity.
NEJM EMBRACA clinical response context PMID:30110579 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to engage apoptosis after PARPi-associated DNA damage (or rapid adaptation) is a core non-response pattern.
FDA TALZENNA label (expected cytotoxic mechanism) (FDA Access Data); PARPi resistance review (MDPI)

REACTOME_ABC_FAMILY_PROTEINS_MEDIATED_TR.description: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters mediate drug efflux and regulate intracellular concentrations of small molecules.
REACTOME_ABC_FAMILY_PROTEINS_MEDIATED_TR.interpretation:
ABC transporter activity can modulate intracellular exposure to anticancer drugs in breast cancer cells, affecting effective drug levels within tumor cells.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Overexpression of ABC transporters decreases intracellular PARP inhibitor levels. For talazoparib, recent work highlights ABCC1 and ABCG2 as key mediators of efflux and resistance; for the PARPi class as a whole, ABCB1/BCRP (ABCG2) are well-established. Thus, baseline ↑ ABC transporter signalling in breast tumors is expected to reduce talazoparib efficacy. (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: ABC transporter upregulation may not involve the relevant efflux pumps for talazoparib in that tumor, so sensitivity can persist.
Reactome R-HSA-382556; MSigDB REACTOME_ABC_FAMILY_PROTEINS_MEDIATED_TRANSPORT (M758) (Reactome); talazoparib–ABC interactions PMID:36430819 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High ABC efflux capacity (notably BCRP/ABCG2 or ABCC family) can lower intracellular PARPi exposure → decreased efficacy (MDR phenotype).
Reactome R-HSA-382556 (Reactome); talazoparib modulates MDR via ABCC1/ABCG2 PMID:36430819 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low efflux transporter activity can increase intracellular talazoparib, amplifying PARP trapping and cytotoxicity.
FDA TALZENNA label (PARP-DNA complexes) (FDA Access Data); Reactome R-HSA-382556 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (orthogonal): Tumors may still be PARPi-resistant due to HRR restoration/DDR rewiring even with low ABC transport signatures.
PARPi resistance review (MDPI); BRCA reversion as resistance PMID:32699032 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Early drug response may still occur before adaptive efflux reaches levels sufficient to blunt exposure (transient sensitivity).
MDR interaction evidence PMID:36430819 (PubMed); Reactome R-HSA-382556 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Acquired resistance can involve adaptive upregulation of efflux transporters (ABCG2/ABCCs) reducing intracellular PARPi.
PMID:36430819 (PubMed); Reactome R-HSA-382556 (Reactome)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (exposure-driven): Persistently low transporter activity supports sustained intracellular drug levels → maintained response.
Reactome R-HSA-382556 (Reactome); FDA TALZENNA label (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Resistance can still arise via HRR restoration or checkpoint adaptations even without efflux upregulation.
BRCA reversion resistance PMID:32699032 (PubMed); PARPi resistance review (MDPI)

REACTOME_ACTIVATION_OF_ATR_IN_RESPONSE_T.description: ATR-mediated checkpoint signaling responds to replication stress by slowing cell cycle progression and coordinating DNA damage responses and repair processes.
REACTOME_ACTIVATION_OF_ATR_IN_RESPONSE_T.interpretation:
Replication-stress checkpoints can influence breast cancer cell survival under genotoxic stress by regulating time for repair and coordinating damage tolerance.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Upregulated ATR–CHK1 signalling allows tumour cells to better tolerate replication stress and repair PARPi-induced lesions, contributing to acquired or de novo PARPi resistance. Multiple models show that PARPi-resistant cells exhibit ↑ ATR activity and that ATR inhibition re-sensitizes them to PARP inhibitors (including in breast/ovarian DNA-repair–deficient settings). (Nature)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: High baseline replication stress can indicate fragile fork dynamics; adding PARP trapping may push cells past tolerance → sensitivity.
Reactome R-HSA-176187; MSigDB M11153 (Reactome); PARP–ATR/CHK1 reliance concept (cross-cancer DDR) PMID:33352723 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong ATR checkpoint competence can stabilize stressed forks and enforce cell-cycle arrest, helping survive PARPi-induced replication stress.
Reactome R-HSA-176187 (Reactome); PARPi increases reliance on ATR/CHK1 (cross-cancer DDR) PMID:33352723 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low ATR activation/checkpoint reserve can impair fork protection/checkpoint response, making PARP trapping more lethal.
Reactome R-HSA-176187 (Reactome); ATR/CHK1 dependency review (DDR rationale) (MDPI)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low replication stress signaling can reflect slow-cycling/low-DDR-demand tumors with less dependence on PARP-mediated repair → reduced PARPi benefit.
Reactome R-HSA-176187 (Reactome); breast PARPi clinical context PMID:30110579 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Marked ATR activation after PARPi can also be a sign of overwhelming fork collapse/DDR overload that proceeds to death (especially in HRD).
FDA TALZENNA label (DNA damage via PARP-DNA complexes) (FDA Access Data); ATR/CHK1 reliance (cross-cancer DDR) PMID:27993965 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PARP inhibition commonly increases ATR/CHK1 dependence; robust ATR signaling can enable survival and is a rationale for ATRi combinations (noting much evidence is cross-cancer but mechanistically transferable).
Reactome R-HSA-176187 (Reactome); PARP→ATR/CHK1 reliance PMID:27993965; PMID:33352723 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (bulk-tissue effect): Sensitive tumors may show reduced ATR-pathway transcripts later due to tumor cell loss; talazoparib does not directly inhibit ATR.
FDA TALZENNA label (targets PARP1/2, not ATR) (FDA Access Data); Reactome R-HSA-176187 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If talazoparib fails to induce meaningful replication stress/DDR engagement, ATR activation remains low and the tumor behaves resistant.
Reactome R-HSA-176187 (Reactome); PARPi mechanism context (FDA Access Data)

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling is a pro-survival and growth pathway that promotes cell survival, proliferation, and can influence DNA repair and apoptotic thresholds.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation:
PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activity contributes to breast cancer cell survival programs and can affect responses to therapies by supporting survival and repair signaling.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- In many breast cancers (TNBC, HR+), PI3K/AKT is upregulated, supporting survival and often maintaining HR competency. Preclinical work in TNBC shows that PI3K inhibition downregulates BRCA1/2, induces HR impairment and sensitizes tumours to PARP inhibition; conversely, intact/high PI3K–AKT signalling tends to sustain HR and survival, favouring relative resistance to single-agent PARPi unless the pathway is co-inhibited. So for baseline tumour state: Up → more resistant; pharmacologic Down (with PI3K/AKT inhibitors) → sensitization. (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HRD/gBRCA breast cancers can still have high PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling; talazoparib response can be driven primarily by HRD despite survival signaling.
NEJM EMBRACA (gBRCA response context) PMID:30110579 (PubMed); MSigDB HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING (M5923) (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K-AKT-mTOR pro-survival signaling can buffer DNA-damage stress and support repair/tolerance programs → relative PARPi resistance.
MSigDB M5923 (GSEA MSigDB); PARPi resistance overview (MDPI)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low PI3K-AKT survival tone can reduce apoptosis thresholds, making PARPi-induced DNA damage more lethal.
MSigDB M5923 (GSEA MSigDB); FDA TALZENNA label (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Very low PI3K-AKT-mTOR can coincide with low proliferation/replication stress, reducing reliance on PARP-mediated repair and limiting PARPi cytotoxicity.
MSigDB M5923 (GSEA MSigDB); breast PARPi overview PMID:29660759 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Tumors may mount a compensatory PI3K-AKT response to DNA damage, but if HRD is profound the compensation is insufficient and sensitivity remains.
FDA TALZENNA label (FDA Access Data); MSigDB M5923 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive PI3K-AKT-mTOR activation can promote survival under PARP trapping and is a known rationale for PI3K/PARP combinations (breast/TNBC shown preclinically).
PI3K↔PARP combination rationale in TNBC/BRCA contexts: PMID:22915752; PMID:22915751 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (signature-level): Effective response with cell-cycle arrest/cell death can manifest as reduced PI3K-AKT-mTOR transcriptional output in tumor bulk.
MSigDB M5923 (GSEA MSigDB); NEJM EMBRACA PMID:30110579 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (orthogonal): Tumors can remain resistant via HRR restoration (BRCA reversion/Shieldin loss) even without PI3K-AKT activation.
BRCA reversion resistance PMID:32699032 (PubMed); Shieldin/53BP1 resistance biology PMID:30224654 (PMC)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: PTEN expression is described as an example of PI3K/AKT pathway inhibition that can sensitize tumors to talazoparib by lowering pro-survival signaling and reducing support for HR capacity.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: BRCA1 loss is described as causing HR deficiency that prevents efficient double-strand break repair, creating synthetic lethality under PARP inhibition and promoting talazoparib sensitivity.
BRCA2 loss is described as causing HR deficiency that prevents efficient double-strand break repair, creating synthetic lethality under PARP inhibition and promoting talazoparib sensitivity.
Defects in PALB2 are described as HR gene defects that reduce efficient double-strand break repair, increasing sensitivity to talazoparib via HR deficiency.
Defects in RAD51C are described as HR gene defects associated with impaired DSB repair capacity, increasing sensitivity to talazoparib.
Defects in RAD51D are described as HR gene defects associated with impaired DSB repair capacity, increasing sensitivity to talazoparib.

ATM is described among HR gene defects linked to reduced efficient DSB repair and increased sensitivity to PARP inhibition; separately, ATR/ATM checkpoint activation is described as opposing talazoparib efficacy.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: ABCB1 (MDR1/P-gp) overexpression is described as exporting talazoparib out of cancer cells, lowering intracellular drug levels and conferring PARP inhibitor resistance.
Overexpression of anti-apoptotic BCL-2 is described as downregulating apoptotic cell death, allowing survival despite DNA damage and reducing talazoparib efficacy.
ATR checkpoint activation is described as slowing the cell cycle and promoting repair; upregulated ATR signaling facilitates survival under PARP inhibition and opposes talazoparib efficacy.
ATM checkpoint pathway activation is described as part of replication-stress/DNA damage checkpoint signaling that provides more time for repair under PARP inhibition, contributing to resistance.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss of 53BP1 (TP53BP1) is described as enabling DNA end resection and HR restoration, which can abrogate PARP inhibitor lethality and confer talazoparib resistance.
Loss of RIF1 is described alongside 53BP1-related factors as enabling restoration of HR capacity (via resumed DNA end resection), contributing to talazoparib resistance.
Downregulation of nucleases such as MRE11 is described as promoting replication fork protection (fork stability), allowing survival under PARP inhibition and contributing to resistance.
Downregulation of nucleases such as MUS81 is described as promoting replication fork protection (fork stability), allowing survival under PARP inhibition and contributing to resistance.
Loss of p53 function is described as impairing apoptosis and checkpoints required for full PARP inhibitor response, thereby blunting talazoparib-induced cell death and contributing to resistance.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-negative disease (both triple-negat: Talazoparib is typically used in HER2-negative disease (both triple-negative and hormone-receptor positive), reflecting its trial populations.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1-mutant (typically basal/TNBC): An analysis of the ABRAZO trial found comparable talazoparib efficacy in BRCA1-mutant (typically basal/TNBC) tumors.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA2-mutant (often luminal): An analysis of the ABRAZO trial found comparable talazoparib efficacy in BRCA2-mutant (often luminal) tumors.

notes: The report describes talazoparib as FDA-approved (October 2018) for germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative advanced/metastatic breast cancer and emphasizes HR deficiency–driven synthetic lethality. Resistance mechanisms described include HR restoration (e.g., via BRCA reversion and loss of end-joining factors such as TP53BP1/RIF1), ABCB1-mediated drug efflux, ATR/ATM checkpoint activation, PI3K/AKT/mTOR pro-survival signaling, impaired apoptosis (e.g., BCL2 overexpression or TP53 loss), and replication fork protection (e.g., via downregulation of nucleases such as MRE11 and MUS81). PTEN loss is described as having complex effects, with PTEN expression cited as an example of PI3K/AKT inhibition that can sensitize to talazoparib.
